title: Export Documentation and Procedural Compliance
summary: The procedural requirements for export have evolved from general statutory declarations to more granular, digitized, and audit-focused requirements. Over time, the focus has shifted from simple bill-of-export filings to the integration of electronic systems, specific utilization declarations (UD/UP), and mandatory electronic security measures for transit.

evolution.procedure: Shifted from manual declarations to digitized, audit-ready, and electronically sealed processes.
evolution.documentation: Increased granularity in reporting raw material utilization and waste ratios.

timeline.change: Established foundational definitions for input-output coefficients and actual duty rates for export-oriented production.

Formalized the requirement for specific supporting documents (L/C, invoices) and introduced standardized definitions for Utilization Permission (UP) and Utilization Declaration (UD) for bonded warehouse exports.
Mandated the use of electronic seals and locks for export-bound containers to ensure supply chain security.
Introduced a standardized reporting form for raw material consumption and waste ratios specifically linked to export orders.

Customs Act 1969: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 1969 for the purpose of these rules.
It serves as the parent legal instrument for interpreting terms not specifically defined within this regulation.
Import Duty: This is defined as the customs duty and regulatory duty paid at the import stage against materials used in the production or manufacturing of exported goods.
Input-Output Coefficient: It refers to the total quantity of inputs, including wastage, consumed in the production of one unit of exported goods.
Actual Rate: This refers to the amount of import duty paid on imported materials, including wastage, used by a manufacturer to produce one unit of a specific exported product.
Deemed Export: This is defined as per the meaning assigned in the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
Bonded Institution: This refers to an establishment licensed to operate as a private warehouse under the provisions of the Customs Act 1969.
Bill of Export: The term refers to the document as defined under the relevant clauses of the Customs Act 1969.
National Board of Revenue: The term Board is defined as the authority established under the National Board of Revenue Order 1972.
Director General (Duty Exemption and Dra: This refers to the official designated under the Customs Act 1969 as responsible for matters concerning duty exemption and drawback.
Export: This refers to the act of exporting as defined under the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 and the Customs Act 1969.
Exporter: An exporter is defined as a person or institution that exports goods either directly to locations outside Bangladesh or to export processing zones, or performs deemed export activities while complying with export policies and central bank regulations.
Date of Export: This is defined as the date on which the bill of export is submitted for the purpose of exportation in accordance with the Customs Act 1969.
Average Rate: This refers to a fixed rate of import duty determined per unit of exported goods produced by a firm or similar firms using the same types of inputs for identical or similar products.

Deemed Export: Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012
Export: Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012

Bill of Lading: This document is a mandatory requirement to be submitted along with the goods declaration during the import process.
Certificate of Origin: This document is a mandatory requirement to be submitted along with the goods declaration during the export process.
National Board of Revenue: The board, along with the government and other relevant departments, has the authority to issue orders from time to time specifying additional documentation requirements for both imports and exports.
Customs Invoice and Documentation: General invoices and packing lists are required for both import and export declarations, along with specific transport documents for imports and commercial contracts for exports.
Export: Exporters must provide specific supporting documents including sales contracts or letters of credit, invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin during the customs declaration process.

Customs Act 2023: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purposes of these rules.
Import Eligibility: Import eligibility is defined as the quantity of raw materials that may be imported under warehousing facilities, determined based on the approved annual production capacity of machinery and the projected consumption of raw materials.
Utilization Permission: Utilization Permission is defined as the authorization issued by the customs authorities to produce goods using duty-free raw materials imported under the warehousing system and properly bonded, in accordance with the provisions of the Customs Act.
Raw Materials: Raw materials are defined as those imported or locally procured in accordance with existing regulations for the purpose of producing goods for export.
Schedule: The term Schedule is defined as any schedule contained within these rules.
Directorate: The term Directorate is defined as the Directorate of Customs Duty Exemption and Drawback.
Input-Output Coefficient: The term Coefficient refers to a declaration approved by the appropriate authority detailing the description and quantity of raw materials required to produce a single unit of finished goods.

Directorate: Directorate of Customs Duty Exemption and Drawback

Customs Act 2023: This law is officially referred to as the Act within these rules.
Utilization Declaration: Defined as a document submitted by the bonded warehouse licensee to customs authorities and certified by a recognized business association, it specifies details such as imported raw materials, production processes, and export contracts under the bonded warehouse system.
It serves as a mandatory declaration of raw materials to be used in production for export under specific sections of the Customs Act.
Raw Materials: These are defined as inputs and intermediate goods imported specifically for the purpose of manufacturing products for export.
Schedule: Refers to any schedule appended to these rules.
Product Owner: Defined as any individual, business entity, group of persons, or association that owns or manages an industrial enterprise.
Bonded Warehouse License: Refers to the party responsible for the bonded facility as defined under the relevant section of the Customs Act.
Warehouse License: Defined as the license granted to an industrial enterprise under the Customs Act for operating a bonded warehouse.
Lien Bank: A commercial bank approved by the licensing authority through which a bonded warehouse licensee conducts all its import-export activities and financial transactions.
Industrial Enterprise: Defined as an export-oriented entity that imports necessary raw materials for the production and export of finished goods.
Direct Export-Oriented Industrial Enterp: An industrial enterprise that exports its entire production of goods to foreign markets.

member_objects.clause_title: ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক এর ব্যবহার
member_objects.resolved_text:
১২। ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক এর ব্যবহার।—(১) কোনো অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটরের caravan এর পণ্য খালাসের লক্ষ্যে আমদানি পণ্যবাহী কন্টেইনার অথবা উক্ত কন্টেইনার বা নৌযান বা অপর কোনো যানবাহন হইতে পণ্য নামাইয়া অন্য কোনো যানবাহনে স্থানান্তর করা হইলে উক্ত যানবাহনে অথবা রপ্তানির লক্ষ্যে বন্দরের উদ্দেশ্যে প্রেরিত পণ্যবাহী যানবাহনে বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, কন্টেইনারে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড কর্তৃক জারীকৃত ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক বিধিমালা অনুসারে ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক আবশ্যিকভাবে ব্যবহার করিতে হইবে।
(২) কোনো অনিবার্য কারণে উক্ত ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক ব্যবস্থা কার্যকর না থাকিলে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড লিখিত আদেশের মাধ্যমে উপ-বিধি (১) এর বিধান শিথিল করিতে পারিবে।
(৩) ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক ব্যবহারের ক্ষেত্রে কোনো ব্যত্যয় ঘটিতেছে কি না তাহা যথোপযুক্ত কাস্টমস কর্মকর্তা এবং অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর সনদপ্রাপ্ত caravan কর্তৃক নিয়মিতভাবে তদারকি করিতে হইবে।

Authorized Economic Operator: An Authorized Economic Operator must ensure the mandatory use of electronic seals and locks on containers or vehicles carrying import or export goods, as per the rules issued by the National Board of Revenue.
Authorized Economic Operators are responsible for regularly monitoring the electronic seal and lock system to detect any irregularities in its application.
Electronic Seal and Lock: The use of electronic seals and locks is mandatory for containers and transport vehicles during the import, transshipment, or transport of goods to ports for export, subject to rules established by the National Board of Revenue.
The National Board of Revenue reserves the authority to issue written orders to temporarily relax the requirement for electronic seals and locks in unavoidable circumstances.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue rules governing the implementation and use of electronic seals and locks.
The board has the legal authority to grant written relaxations to the mandatory electronic seal and lock requirements when unavoidable conditions arise.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: Appropriate customs officials are required to regularly supervise the use of electronic seals and locks to ensure there are no deviations from the prescribed compliance procedures.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue mandates this declaration form to be completed for the disclosure of raw materials required in the production of export goods.
This form serves as a standardized regulatory requirement to monitor input-output coefficients for export-oriented manufacturing.
Value Added Tax: The declaration requires the disclosure of the Value Added Tax registration number for the manufacturing establishment to ensure compliance with tax administration procedures.
Export: This form is associated with specific export orders and requires the declaration of all raw materials consumed in the production process to verify utilization and waste ratios.
Commissioner of Customs: The declaration form requires countersignature by the Commissioner of Customs to formalize the approval of the declared input-output requirements for the manufacturer.
